# Base image with OpenMPI, libfabric for AWS EFA, and Flux Framework on Ubuntu 22.04 ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Prevents interactive prompts during package installation
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies for LAMMPS
# ca-certificates is included for secure network communications (e.g., git clone)
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the build process
WORKDIR /opt

# Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code
RUN git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git

# Create a build directory and move into it
WORKDIR /opt/lammps/build

# Configure the LAMMPS build with CMake
# - Use mpicc and mpicxx as the C and CXX compilers for MPI compatibility
# - Enable the REAXFF package as required
# - Enable the KSPACE package for FFT calculations, common in HPC simulations
RUN cmake ../cmake \
    -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
    -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
    -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
    -D PKG_KSPACE=yes

# Compile LAMMPS using all available processor cores
RUN make -j$(nproc)

# Copy the compiled lmp executable to a system location on the PATH
RUN cp ./lmp /usr/local/bin/

# Set the final working directory for running simulations
WORKDIR /opt/lammps-reax

# Copy the example files for the reaxff/HNS case into the working directory
RUN cp /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS/* .

# Clean up the build source to reduce image size
RUN rm -rf /opt/lammps

# Verify that the 'lmp' executable is in the system PATH
RUN which lmp

# This MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a LAMMPS simulation on AWS.
# It is configured for an ARM-based CPU instance with EFA networking,
# leveraging the Flux Operator to manage the distributed job.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name for the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # Deploy to the default Kubernetes namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # Size of the MiniCluster (in pods/nodes). The job will start with one node.
  size: 1
  # Maximum size for bursting or scaling, up to 4 nodes as requested.
  maxSize: 4
  # The 'tasks' field is intentionally not set. This allows Flux to automatically
  # launch one MPI rank per available CPU on the node, fulfilling the
  # "run on all processes of one node" requirement in a portable way.

  # Keep pods running after the job finishes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Configure strict logging to fail the job on any Flux framework error.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configuration section.
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the Flux broker, as required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    # Configuration for the Flux view container, used by the operator.
    container:
      # Use the ARM build of the Flux view container as requested.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disable the Flux sidecar container. Flux will be injected into and run
      # directly within the main application container for better performance.
      disable: true

  # The main application container definition. Only one container is specified.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by `flux run`. The operator prepends `flux run`.
      # This command runs a specific LAMMPS ReaxFF simulation for HNS.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher pod.
      launcher: false
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled before running.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # Set the working directory to where the input files are located inside the container.
      workingDir: /opt/lammps/examples/reaxff/HNS
      # Resource requests and limits for AWS-specific hardware (EFA networking).
      # No CPU or memory limits are set, allowing the pod to be "Burstable" and use
      # all available node CPU/memory resources.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

      # Disable the Flux sidecar container. Flux will be injected into and run

      disable: true

  # The main application container definition. Only one container is specified.
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to be executed by `flux run`. The operator prepends `flux run`.

      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # This is the main application container, not a launcher pod.
      launcher: false

      # CORRECTED: Set the working directory to where the input files are located

# This corrected and scaled-up MiniCluster manifest is designed to run a larger
# LAMMPS simulation across multiple high-performance ARM-based AWS nodes.
# It incorporates performance optimizations for AWS EFA networking and targets
# specific instance types for consistent performance.
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # Name for the MiniCluster resource.
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  # Deploy to the default Kubernetes namespace.
  namespace: default
spec:
  # --- Job Scale and Placement ---
  # Number of pods (nodes) for the MiniCluster.
  size: 4
  # Maximum number of pods for bursting; set to the initial size.
  maxSize: 4
  # Number of MPI tasks to run per pod. This should match the vCPU count of the target instance.
  tasks: 64

  # Pod specification to control scheduling.
  pod:
    # Schedule pods only on nodes with the specified AWS instance type.
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge

  # --- Job Control and Logging ---
  # Keep pods running after the job finishes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false
  # Configure strict logging to fail the job on any Flux framework error.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # --- Flux Framework Configuration ---
  flux:
    # Specify the architecture for the Flux broker, as required for ARM instances.
    arch: "arm"
    # Configuration for the Flux view container, used by the operator.
    container:

      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
      # Disable the Flux sidecar container. Flux will be injected into and run
      # directly within the main application container for better performance.
      disable: true

  # --- Application Container Definition ---
  containers:
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
      # The command to run, scaled up for a larger, multi-node simulation.
      # The Flux Operator prepends the necessary `flux run` invocation.
      command: lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
      # Per instructions, this container is a worker in the MiniCluster, not just a job launcher.
      launcher: false
      # Ensure the latest version of the container is always pulled before running.
      imagePullPolicy: Always
      # The working directory where the input files are located inside the container.
      workingDir: /opt/lammps-reax

      # Environment variables required for MPI to use the high-speed AWS EFA interconnect.
      environment:
        FI_PROVIDER: efa
        FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: "1"
        OMPI_MCA_pml: cm
        OMPI_MCA_mtl: ofi

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS-specific hardware (EFA networking).
      # No CPU or memory limits are set, allowing the pod to be "Burstable".
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: "1"

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-aws-cpu
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 20 -v y 20 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    environment:
      FI_EFA_USE_DEVICE_RDMA: '1'
      FI_PROVIDER: efa
      OMPI_MCA_mtl: ofi
      OMPI_MCA_pml: cm
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: '1'
    workingDir: /opt/lammps-reax
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  maxSize: 4
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST set environment variables for MPI to use EFA with libfabric.
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
